title: Pitch: Quillon Data (Series A) — Foxglove first meeting
body:
Quillon Data — Series A pitch (first meeting)

Company overview
- Quillon builds an audit-grade data lineage layer for regulated mid-market banks. Live with 9 paying customers, ~$1.4M ARR, 140% net revenue retention.
- Freya founded the company in 2024 after six years running data platform teams at Harbourline Systems. Her co-founder and CTO, Aldo Reyes, couldn't join today (customer onboarding in Rotterdam) — he was previously a principal engineer at Harbourline as well, and by Freya's account wrote most of the current ingestion engine himself.
- Raising $12M at a proposed $55M pre. Seed was led by angel Nils Ostrander of Cobalt Ferry Capital, who still sits on the board and is not taking pro-rata this round.

What stood out
- Sales motion is founder-led but repeatable: 3 of the last 4 deals closed without Freya on the final call.
- Gross margin 81%, burn ~$210K/month, 19 months runway pre-raise.
- Compliance wedge is defensible — two customers cited the audit-export feature as the reason they switched from spreadsheet-based tracking.

Concerns / open questions
- Concentration: top 2 customers are 44% of ARR.
- Engineering team is only 7 people; key-person risk around Aldo Reyes is real and Freya acknowledged it directly.
- Nils Ostrander passing on pro-rata needs a clean explanation — Freya says Cobalt Ferry is winding down its angel vehicle, worth verifying.

Action items
- [ ] Dana: run founder references on Freya — start with her former colleagues at Harbourline Systems.
- [ ] Dana: intro call with Aldo Reyes within 2 weeks (technical deep dive).
- [ ] Dana: sound out Sam Okafor at Halcyon on co-investing $2–3M — this feels like his kind of infra deal.
- [ ] Freya to send: cohort retention data, security audit summary, cap table.
- [ ] Schedule partner-meeting discussion for the 22nd if references come back clean.

title: Reference call: Freya Lindqvist (Quillon Data)
body:
Reference call re: Freya Lindqvist, CEO of Quillon Data

Reference: Marcus Deng, VP of Engineering at Harbourline Systems — was Freya's direct manager for four years and worked alongside Aldo Reyes for six. Off-list reference sourced through my own network, not from Freya's list.

On Freya
- "Top 1% of people I've managed. She ran our data platform group through a re-platforming that touched every product line and didn't lose a single senior engineer."
- Strengths: relentless prioritization, unusually good at hiring, communicates bad news early. Marcus said customers asked for her by name during escalations.
- Development areas: can under-delegate under pressure. Marcus noted she took on the regulator-facing work herself for too long before hiring for it. Says she has visibly improved since starting Quillon.
- Would he back her? "I put personal money into the seed round. That's my answer."

On the Freya/Aldo dynamic
- Marcus rates Aldo Reyes as the strongest systems engineer he's worked with, but confirms the key-person risk: "If Aldo left, they'd feel it for two quarters." He believes Aldo is deeply committed — turned down a staff role at a large cloud vendor last year.
- No interpersonal red flags; they disagreed openly at Harbourline and it stayed productive.

On the Cobalt Ferry question
- Marcus independently confirmed that Nils Ostrander is winding down the Cobalt Ferry angel vehicle for personal reasons — nothing to do with Quillon. Two other Cobalt Ferry portfolio founders got the same message this spring.

Cross-check
- Marcus suggested one more reference: Sana Iqbal, former CFO at Harbourline Systems, who sat on the internal committee that funded Freya's platform budget. He offered to make the intro.

Action items
- [ ] Dana: take the Sana Iqbal reference call before the partner meeting on the 22nd.
- [ ] Dana: log both references in the Quillon deal file for Jonas Berg to fold into the Nordwind co-invest memo if we bring them in.
- [ ] Mark founder-reference workstream green pending the Iqbal call.

title: Foxglove Capital — Monday partner meeting
body:
Foxglove Capital — Monday partner meeting, 22 June 2026

1. Quillon Data (Series A) — decision discussion
- Dana walked through the deal: $12M at $55M pre, we'd take $6–7M and lead.
- References on Freya Lindqvist are strong. Marcus Deng at Harbourline Systems gave one of the most emphatic founder references Dana has heard, and the Sana Iqbal call on Friday corroborated it, including on budget discipline.
- Rob pushed on customer concentration (top 2 = 44% of ARR). Agreed we need one customer call each with the two anchor accounts before issuing a term sheet.
- Key-person risk on the CTO: mitigation is a retention grant for Aldo Reyes structured at close. Elena Ruiz at Bright & Field can draft alongside the main docs.
- Co-invest: Sam Okafor at Halcyon verbally interested for $2.5M. Maya Chen at Nordwind also asked for a look after hearing about the deal at the Meridian LP dinner — decide by Wednesday whether we want one co-investor or two.
- VOTE: proceed to term sheet, conditional on the two customer calls. Unanimous.

2. Portfolio review — Bracken Tide Energy
- Q2 numbers in: revenue 8% ahead of plan, but hardware margin slipped to 31%. Rob to sit in on their next ops review.

3. Fund II pipeline
- Priya Nair's team at Meridian Wealth confirmed for the September AGM; Tom Voss asked for the co-invest track record pack two weeks ahead. Dana owns it.

Action items
- [ ] Dana: customer reference calls for Quillon anchor accounts — complete by Friday.
- [ ] Dana: draft term sheet with Elena Ruiz, including the Aldo Reyes retention grant.
- [ ] Dana: confirm allocation split with Sam Okafor; give Maya Chen an answer by Wednesday.
- [ ] Rob: attend Bracken Tide ops review; report back next Monday.
- [ ] Dana: start the Meridian co-invest pack ahead of the September AGM.
